svg.text: Tiny example in standard matrix form
y = relu(x · A1 + b1) · A2 + b2 with A = Wᵀ · rows of x = tokens · 2 tokens, d = 4, ffn = 4, TP = 2 · values from tiny_example.py
worked entry: highlighted row · highlighted column = highlighted cell
every product below is (row i of the left matrix) · (column j of the right matrix)
of A2; sum over own units
g (forward): all-reduce SUM across the 2 ranks
G = dL/dy is the same on both ranks; Xᵀ means transpose
f (backward): all-reduce SUM across the 2 ranks
Exact check that must be False:
rank 0's dx_r alone ≠ dense dx. Without f's backward all-reduce, each rank keeps only the paths through its own units.
